cues.text: Welcome to Citizen of the Week, where ordinary people achieve extraordinary levels of not getting involved. Nominations are collected automatically.
This week's finalist watched his neighbor's house collapse, checked the evacuation app, and reported an excellent user experience.
Our next nominee found an unfamiliar card in the street and handed it to Security without reading a single word. A beautiful example of functional literacy.
One resident corrected her own eyewitness account before officials asked. <break time="0.45s" /> She has been promoted to witness for the prosecution.
And a special commendation for the citizen who noticed an unmarked van, smiled politely, and made room at the curb.
The winner of Citizen of the Week has agreed to donate the prize money to the department that selected them. That's what we call community.
Honorable mention goes to a resident who reported his own suspicious silence. Investigators described the conversation as highly productive.
Remember, anyone can become Citizen of the Week. Some people are entered more than once, under different names.
Welcome to Who Wants to Be Compliant? Four choices, one correct answer, and a sponsor who knows which one.
Question one! Who owns the information collected by your household appliances? A: you. B: the manufacturer. C: a trusted partner. The correct answer is: thank you for participating.
Quick-fire round! Is compulsory participation voluntary? Yes, yes with enthusiasm, or yes after reviewing the terms? <break time="0.45s" /> All three advance to the next round.
A viewer asks whether the quiz can be skipped. Congratulations! That was our trick question. The viewer has already qualified.
What is the safest response to an unexplained government vehicle? Keep walking, stop walking, or report the walking? Our judges accept any response submitted in advance.
Tonight's jackpot is a lifetime exemption from unnecessary questions. Winners receive a certificate, which is itself a necessary question.
Our contestant used the phone-a-friend lifeline. The friend's phone answered on behalf of both parties. A brilliant team effort.
Another flawless game! Remember, on Who Wants to Be Compliant, you can't lose. The losses are processed by another department.
It's election night on Democracy Deluxe! Stay for the count, the charts, and the moving tribute to a winner we can already confirm.
The public has narrowed the field to a remarkable range of approved opinions, from strongly recommended to very strongly recommended.
Our interactive voting line is open! Press one to support the outcome. Press two to support the process. All other keys are comments.
This evening's exit poll has achieved a hundred percent accuracy. It was conducted entirely inside the ballot-printing facility.
We asked citizens what mattered most: freedom, security, or convenient billing. Our sponsor was deeply moved by their answers and selected security.
The undecided voters have finally decided. They will be moved to a separate statistical category with no effect on the result.
The opposition has made an important contribution to democracy by appearing in the official photograph. Their objections were cropped for clarity.
Democracy Deluxe will return after a brief emergency. Emergency extensions are determined by popular demand from the board.
This is The Consensus Challenge, the only quiz where the experts agree before we've finished asking the question.
Round one! Can you tell the peer-reviewed study from the shareholder presentation? Hint: the shareholder presentation has fewer footnotes and a better catering budget.
Follow the science! Our contestants are following it down the hallway, past the ethics office, and into a private investor briefing.
Tonight's hypothesis is officially evidence-based. The evidence will be delivered as soon as procurement completes its internal review.
A caller has requested the raw data. Wonderful curiosity! Our help desk has sent them a beautifully illustrated summary of why they don't need it.
In a stunning display of independence, all five panelists arrived at the same conclusion. The sixth panelist arrived at the airport and was turned away.
Our audience has correctly identified the expert by his credentials, the approved backdrop, and the tiny logo on the coffee mug.
That's all for The Consensus Challenge. Stay tuned for tomorrow's new findings, which will have been true all along.
EULA Bingo is back! Fill an entire card with permissions you didn't know you granted, and win one additional permission.
Today's first square: perpetual retention. Your grandmother had the family albums. Your toaster has the family's movement history.
Eyes down for our bonus square: legitimate interest! Nobody knows whose interest, but the lawyers look absolutely thrilled.
A player selected Decline All. That's a rare one! The system recorded her preference and opened the full terms in a new window.
Our next number is thirty-seven: the number of third parties who became first parties while you were reading the consent screen.
We've reached the blackout round! Every box is ticked, every option is grey, and the prize is continued access to your own front door.
The winner receives a handwritten copy of their privacy agreement. For security, the handwriting will be replaced with a QR code.
Thanks for playing EULA Bingo. Your attendance has already been shared with our affiliates, including those who don't exist yet.
Welcome to Neighborhood Watch-Along! The camera never blinks, so we don't have to worry about missing your little moments.
Our live mystery tonight: who entered the empty street after curfew? Was it a trespasser, an authorized patrol, or the person who wrote the curfew?
Look closely at this harmless shadow near the doorway. If it belongs to you, congratulations: you've identified yourself for our prize department.
A resident's refrigerator detected a three-second pause before breakfast. The neighborhood voted to classify it as suspicious contemplation.
We've brought back audience voting! Tap the face you recognize. The faces will be retained after the program ends.
That unmarked vehicle is our mystery guest. We won't reveal the driver, because the driver knows who you are.
Our caller says there are no cameras on her street. <break time="0.45s" /> That's exactly what the camera report says as well.
Neighborhood Watch-Along is brought to you by Smart Dust. We're everywhere in the community, especially between the community.
Welcome to The Founder Knows Best, where democracy gets a performance review and the chief executive takes the throne without leaving his ergonomic chair.
Tonight's design challenge: build a nation with the customer service of a cable company and the accountability of a private island.
Our founder explains that voting is an outdated interface. Now every citizen gets a login, a dashboard, and the opportunity to renew their contract.
The shareholder council has approved freedom of movement for all premium residents. Standard users may enjoy freedom of scrolling.
Our meritocracy is open to everyone. The qualifying round takes place before birth, and winners inherit their entry fees.
A question from the audience: who watches the sovereign? Excellent question! The sovereign's venture capital partners are watching very closely.
This week's constitutional amendment reduces the number of constitutional amendments requiring approval. It's what we call frictionless government.
You've been watching The Founder Knows Best. Next week: why your town hall is now a co-working space with armed receptionists.
Welcome to The Price Is Permitted! Guess the price of everyday necessities before your wallet decides whether you deserve them.
First prize: a loaf of bread. Retail value, three credits. Purchase eligibility, twenty-seven variables. Our contestant is missing one approved smile.
We've got a special on freedom! It's available in three easy installments and cannot be transferred, inherited, or spent outside your designated district.
Spin the wheel! Food, fuel, or personal travel? <break time="0.45s" /> The wheel has landed on risk assessment. What a popular category.
A contestant tried to tip the cashier in cash. The studio lights went red, and the cashier received a valuable training opportunity.
The bonus round is Reverse Shopping: the less you buy, the more we learn about what prevented you.
Tonight's grand prize is debt forgiveness! The debt remains, but our app will stop calling it a debt until Thursday.
Thank you for playing The Price Is Permitted. All winnings expire if the terms of your personality change.
Welcome to Memory Makeover! We take the troubling news you remember and give it the finish it deserves.
Our first before-and-after features a collapsed apartment block. Before: rubble. After: a sustainable open-plan view. The tenants are still in post-production.
Do you remember the blackout? Of course you do! Our new archive has restored the electricity to every official photograph.
This caller insists her street used to have a library. Good news: the building remains in our files as a successful digital learning space.
Today's makeover challenge is a missing person. We can't bring the person back, but we can give the absence a more inclusive name.
Our archivist found two contradictory eyewitness accounts. For a seamless result, we selected the one already printed on the banner.
Everyone loves the new timeline! It contains twelve fewer emergencies and an unexpectedly large number of product launches.
Memory Makeover is sponsored by YesterdayPlus. Because the future shouldn't have to apologize for the past.
You're watching The Happiness Index, where we measure your joy so you can stop pretending to feel it yourself.
Today's most improved citizen raised their happiness score by smiling at a security checkpoint. Facial discomfort has been logged as enthusiasm.
Here's our wellness tip: if the world outside is upsetting, turn off the window and consult the official mood forecast.
Let's check the leaderboard! First place is held by an anonymous account with excellent benefits and no documented physical body.
The audience has reported a drop in morale. Our researchers fixed the questionnaire. Morale is up forty percent.
Your employer has purchased a happiness subscription for you. Cancellation requires a written statement that you are unhappy, which lowers your score.
Our weekly winner receives a full weekend of rest, subject to productivity monitoring and weekday availability.
That's The Happiness Index. Remember, your smile is yours. The measurements belong to us.
It's time for Public Enemy Makeover, the show that turns every unexplained stranger into the face of a national conversation.
Our mystery contestant has collected another unauthorized card. Is that a hobby, a political movement, or a merchandising opportunity? Stay tuned.
A building has disappeared, and the authorities have a new suspect. The before picture is classified. The after picture is available on a commemorative mug.
Tonight's challenge: identify the public enemy using only a coat, a blurry silhouette, and an increasingly confident voice-over.
Our studio audience has voted the fugitive a national disgrace. The advertising department has voted them an excellent brand partner.
Security has issued a fresh warning: do not approach the suspect. Fans are advised that autographs are prohibited within the cordon.
An exciting twist! Yesterday's terrorist is today's urban-renewal pioneer. The category changed while our commercial was playing.
Don't miss Public Enemy Makeover. The search continues, even when the story says the suspect has already been found.
Welcome to The Great Normalize-Off! Our panel has sixty seconds to turn a public disaster into an award-winning lifestyle announcement.
Round one! A bridge is gone. The planning department calls it a pedestrian-friendly gap. The sponsor calls it an invitation to upgrade your commute.
The winning entry for a missing neighborhood is: temporary reduction in urban density. Bonus points for the word temporary.
A factory exploded near the town square. The publicist calls it a new approach to open-air manufacturing. The jury is delighted by the transparency.
Now for our speed round: sirens become sound baths; barricades become wellness borders; missing witnesses become data minimization.
Tonight's final challenge: explain why the cameras went dark. Our contestant says privacy. Security says scheduled maintenance. Both earn a prize.
The audience says it saw the incident. The judges say it saw an opportunity. Only the judges' answer fits on the billboard.
Thank you for watching The Great Normalize-Off. Nothing happened, and the winners will be recognized at the site of the event.
And after this brief commercial break: a democracy special brought to you by the people who wrote the ballot.
Coming up on Brave New World News: one missing district, three successful narratives, and absolutely no outstanding questions.
Vote now for tonight's most convincing explanation! Your vote may be retained for training and is not required to influence the outcome.
Our studio poll is open. We can assure you that your answer will remain anonymous until it becomes useful.
A round of applause for our studio audience of everyday citizens, whose attendance was selected by an independent algorithm.
The opinions expressed by our audience are not necessarily the opinions they had before entering the building.
Thank you for that spontaneous applause. The applause signs have now been switched off. Please continue.
The Brave New World News truth hotline is open twenty-four hours a day. Calls will be answered by whatever you need to hear.
It's the final round! The contestant is free to choose the answer, provided the answer has already been cleared.
We interrupt this program with a correction to the announcement we haven't made yet.
Consume. Believe. Obey. <break time="0.45s" /> And now, back to the game.
This is Brave New World News. The audience has been wonderful. Their profiles will be reviewed overnight.
